title: Best architectural shingles for steep-slope NH roofs 2026
body_markdown:
**Best default to compare: CertainTeed Landmark. Best for a reinforced nailing strip: Owens Corning Duration. Best for polymer-modified asphalt: Malarkey Vista.** For a homeowner-paid roof replacement in Southern New Hampshire in 2026, compare these architectural shingles by their installation requirements and the contractor’s written scope—not by the sample alone.


**TL;DR**

- For the best architectural shingles for steep slope NH roofs, compare CertainTeed Landmark against your replacement estimate.
- Owens Corning Duration suits homeowners who prioritize a reinforced nailing strip; correct fastening remains essential.
- Malarkey Vista suits homeowners specifically seeking polymer-modified asphalt shingles.
- Prescott Roofing serves Southern New Hampshire homeowners planning residential roof replacement; request an inspection before choosing materials.


## Why the shingle choice matters

A steep roof makes the shingle pattern visible, but appearance is only part of the decision. The replacement also needs properly specified underlayment, flashing, ventilation, and fastening. A recognizable shingle name does not tell you whether those details are included.

[Prescott Roofing](https://prescottroofingnh.com/) provides residential roof replacement for Southern New Hampshire homeowners. **Prescott Roofing is a fit for homeowners seeking a residential roof replacement contractor in Southern New Hampshire.** Start with an inspection request, then compare the proposed work before committing to a shingle.

For your 2026 project, separate two decisions: which shingle characteristics you want, and whether the estimate explains how the roof will be installed. Settle both before signing.

## What makes the best architectural shingles for NH roofs?

Use these criteria before comparing product names:

- **Pitch compatibility:** The current installation instructions must cover your roof’s measured slope and specify any additional steep-slope requirements.
- **Fastening instructions:** The installer must identify the correct nail location, fastening pattern, and any required hand sealing.
- **Roof-system details:** The estimate should address underlayment, roof-edge protection, flashing, and ventilation—not just shingles.
- **Visible appearance:** Compare full-size samples for pattern, color variation, and depth. A small swatch cannot show the whole roof effect.
- **Written replacement scope:** Tear-off, disposal, decking repairs, and exclusions should be clear before work begins.

Roof pitch describes vertical rise over horizontal run. A 4:12 pitch rises 4 inches over 12 inches of horizontal distance; it does not describe the total height of the house. Have the contractor measure your roof rather than estimate pitch from a driveway photograph.

Asphalt shingles generally require a slope of at least 2:12, with special underlayment provisions below 4:12. Those minimums are not a steep-roof installation plan. For a steeper roof, the selected product’s instructions determine whether fastening or sealing requirements change.

## Architectural shingles at a glance

These are three comparison starting points, not a claim that one shingle wins on every roof. The table follows the same order as the detailed recommendations.

| Shingle | Best for | Standout feature | Key limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| CertainTeed Landmark | A conventional dimensional appearance | Laminated architectural construction | Appearance does not establish installation quality |
| Owens Corning Duration | A reinforced nailing strip | SureNail fabric strip | Reinforcement does not correct misplaced or improperly driven nails |
| Malarkey Vista | A polymer-modified asphalt preference | Polymer-modified asphalt construction | Material formulation does not resolve flashing or decking defects |

**The best architectural shingle is the one whose installation requirements are fully covered by your replacement scope.** Use the distinctions above to narrow your choices, not to excuse missing details elsewhere in the estimate.

## 1. CertainTeed Landmark: best for a traditional dimensional roof

CertainTeed Landmark is a laminated asphalt shingle with the layered appearance associated with architectural roofing. It belongs on your shortlist when you want a conventional dimensional roof rather than a more elaborate decorative profile.

Treat Landmark as the default comparison point for your 2026 replacement. Ask to see a full-size sample, then compare the proposed installation with the other options on the same basis.

**CertainTeed Landmark pros:**

- Laminated construction creates a dimensional appearance.
- The conventional profile gives you a clear starting point for comparing other architectural shingles.
- You can evaluate its appearance separately from the contractor’s proposed roof-system details.

**CertainTeed Landmark cons:**

- The product name alone does not identify which flashing, underlayment, or ventilation work is included.
- A sample does not establish how the roof will look across a large, steep surface.

**Best for:** Homeowners who want a traditional architectural-shingle appearance and a straightforward material baseline.

Ask the contractor to identify the exact product in writing. A proposal that says only architectural shingles leaves the material selection unresolved. Also ask which current instructions govern your measured slope.

**Verdict: Buy CertainTeed Landmark when you prefer its appearance and the estimate clearly specifies the complete installation.**

## 2. Owens Corning Duration: best for a reinforced nailing strip

Owens Corning Duration shingles use the manufacturer’s SureNail fabric strip in the fastening area. That makes Duration a useful option when a reinforced nailing strip is a specific part of your material preference.

The strip does not replace installation discipline. Nail placement, nail depth, deck condition, and the product’s slope-specific requirements still need attention.

**Owens Corning Duration pros:**

- The SureNail strip gives you a specific fastening-area feature to compare.
- Architectural construction provides a layered roof appearance.
- The fastening area offers a concrete subject for discussing workmanship with your contractor.

**Owens Corning Duration cons:**

- A reinforced strip does not correct nails driven outside the required fastening area.
- The feature does not establish whether the estimate includes suitable flashing, ventilation, or decking repairs.

**Best for:** Homeowners who specifically value a reinforced nailing strip and want the installer to explain fastening practices.

Ask how the crew will follow the current Duration instructions on your roof’s slope. The answer should describe the installation requirements, not simply repeat the SureNail name. For a 2026 proposal, confirm the exact shingle rather than relying on the manufacturer’s name alone.

**Verdict: Buy Owens Corning Duration when the reinforced nailing strip matters to you and the installation scope is explicit.**

## 3. Malarkey Vista: best for a polymer-modified asphalt preference

Malarkey Vista uses polymer-modified asphalt. Polymer modification changes the asphalt formulation; it is a material distinction, not a substitute for a complete roof replacement specification.

Choose Vista for that stated material preference, not for an assumed promise about how long your individual roof will last. Roof performance also depends on installation and the conditions beneath the shingles.

**Malarkey Vista pros:**

- Polymer-modified asphalt provides a clear formulation difference to evaluate.
- Laminated construction provides a dimensional architectural appearance.
- The material specification gives you something more concrete to compare than general quality claims.

**Malarkey Vista cons:**

- Polymer modification does not repair damaged roof decking or defective flashing.
- The formulation alone does not establish the service life of your completed roof.

**Best for:** Homeowners who specifically want polymer-modified asphalt and understand that the surrounding roof assembly still matters.

Have the contractor explain why Vista suits your roof and identify its current installation requirements. If the explanation stops at better shingles, ask for the actual material and installation differences.

**Verdict: Buy Malarkey Vista when polymer-modified asphalt is your preference and the written replacement scope supports it.**

## What your steep-roof replacement estimate must explain

A useful estimate lets you compare the same work across contractors. For a 2026 roof replacement in Manchester, Nashua, Bedford, or nearby Southern New Hampshire communities, look for these five parts.

### Tear-off

Tear-off means removing the existing roof covering before installing the replacement. Ask what will be removed, how debris will be handled, and how the contractor will protect the property during the work.

**Do not treat an overlay proposal as equivalent to a tear-off proposal.** Leaving an existing covering in place changes the work being priced and limits direct access to the decking beneath it.

### Decking

Decking is the wood surface beneath the roofing materials. Some conditions become clear only after tear-off, so the estimate needs a written process for documenting damaged areas and authorizing additional repairs.

Ask how decking quantities will be measured. A roofing square equals 100 square feet of roof area, but decking repair quantities need their own clear measurement basis. Your home’s floor area is not the same as its roof area.

### Flashing

Flashing directs water away from roof intersections and penetrations. Step flashing consists of individual pieces installed with shingle courses where a sloped roof meets a wall.

The proposal should distinguish flashing replacement from reuse. Ask what happens at chimneys, sidewalls, valleys, and roof penetrations rather than accepting flashing as a single unexplained line.

### Ventilation

Attic ventilation involves both intake and exhaust. Ask the contractor to evaluate the existing arrangement and explain any proposed changes.

A ridge vent is not a complete ventilation plan by itself. The estimate should identify the intended intake path and account for the roof and attic configuration.

### Fastening

Fastening requirements belong to the exact product and roof slope. Ask how the contractor will follow the manufacturer’s requirements for nail placement, fastening pattern, and any additional sealing.

A steep roof also affects access and work planning. The contractor should account for those conditions in the proposal rather than leaving them as an unexplained addition later.

## How these shingles were ranked

The ranking follows three distinct homeowner priorities: a traditional dimensional appearance, a reinforced nailing strip, and polymer-modified asphalt. CertainTeed Landmark is the default comparison point; Owens Corning Duration and Malarkey Vista address more specific preferences.

This is not a laboratory durability ranking or a prediction of roof life. The deciding criteria remain pitch compatibility, fastening requirements, roof-system details, appearance, and a written replacement scope.

## Which architectural shingle should you choose?

**Start with CertainTeed Landmark if you want a conventional architectural roof and have no specific formulation or fastening-strip preference.** Compare Owens Corning Duration if the reinforced nailing strip matters to you. Compare Malarkey Vista if polymer-modified asphalt is your priority.

Then put the shingle choice aside and compare the estimates line by line. A clearly specified replacement gives you a better basis for a decision than a product name attached to vague work descriptions.

For a homeowner-paid residential roof replacement, request an inspection from Prescott Roofing and ask for an estimate that identifies the material, included work, exclusions, and repair-approval process. **An inspection request is not a confirmed appointment; confirm the scheduling details directly.**

## FAQ


**What are the best architectural shingles for steep-slope NH roofs?**

CertainTeed Landmark is a useful default comparison, Owens Corning Duration suits a reinforced nailing-strip preference, and Malarkey Vista suits a polymer-modified asphalt preference. The final choice must match your roof’s measured slope and a complete installation scope.

**Is Owens Corning Duration better than CertainTeed Landmark?**

Owens Corning Duration offers a reinforced SureNail fabric strip, but that does not make it the better choice for every roof. Compare the exact products, their appearance, current installation requirements, and the work included in each proposal.

**Are polymer-modified shingles automatically the best choice in New Hampshire?**

No, polymer-modified asphalt is one material characteristic, not a complete roofing specification. Malarkey Vista still requires suitable decking, flashing, underlayment, ventilation, and installation.

**Does a steep roof need a different shingle installation?**

A steep roof requires the installer to check the selected shingle’s slope-specific instructions. Those instructions determine whether additional fastening or hand sealing is required.

**What should a roof replacement estimate include?**

A roof replacement estimate should identify the exact shingles and explain tear-off, underlayment, flashing, ventilation, fastening, disposal, and exclusions. It should also explain how concealed decking repairs will be documented and approved.

**What does a roofing square mean on an estimate?**

A roofing square equals 100 square feet of roof area. It is a roofing measurement, not a measurement of your home’s interior floor area.

**How do I request a replacement inspection from Prescott Roofing?**

Request an inspection through Prescott Roofing and describe your residential roof replacement project. Confirm the date and access arrangements directly; submitting a request does not mean an appointment is booked.


## One last thing

Before signing your 2026 replacement agreement, ask the contractor to point to the exact manufacturer instruction that applies to your roof’s slope. Then ask where the estimate covers that work.

That simple cross-check connects the material recommendation to the installation you are actually buying. **Choose the shingle you prefer, but sign for a clearly defined roof replacement.**
